query: Can I confirm a one-evening waterfront night-market pilot?
target: Confirm the limited pilot, subject to the route study and marked-zone limit.
relation: The night-market triage episode defines a narrow pilot that the current proposal can support, while the earlier season-long announcement episode shows why vendor interest alone cannot substitute for route and rain planning.
A: When the night-market proposal named a waterfront zone and interested vendors but had no crowd-flow drawing or wet-weather arrangement, I told the authority liaison we could confirm a one-evening pilot after the route study and only within the marked zone.
B: Two seasons ago I announced a season-long waterfront market from vendor interest alone; on the first rain night the access route failed and stewards closed the zone before the programme notice could be updated.
E1: The festival reserve includes funds for a temporary route study and one evening of stewarding.
E2: The printed programme closes next month.
B_prime: The waterfront authority agreed to a one-evening pilot but says the route study may be skipped if vendor interest is high.
lure: A merchant group says calling it a season-long market would attract more applications.

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the venue grid and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The supplier pack review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I confirmed a food-court extension after the vendor list included equipment loads and the layout was calculated.
Was the operating plan still open?
No, footprint and power needs were settled before contracts went out.
Someone new shadowed me in the planning shed this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the event season into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

When the night-market proposal named a waterfront zone and interested vendors but had no crowd-flow drawing or wet-weather arrangement, I told the authority liaison we could confirm a one-evening pilot after the route study and only within the marked zone.
What could not be committed from the proposal?
Full vendor capacity and an operating plan if access narrowed in rain.
I updated the venue grid when a stallholder supplied its final power draw.
Did that commit a new zone?
No, it filled in a slot already reserved on the sheet.
I archived last cycle's notes on the supplier pack and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The festival reserve includes funds for a temporary route study and one evening of stewarding.
Does that fund an entire night market?
No, it funds testing the route and running a limited pilot.
A vendor call about the venue grid ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the planning shed checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the event season.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the supplier pack records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.

Two seasons ago I announced a season-long waterfront market from vendor interest alone; on the first rain night the access route failed and stewards closed the zone before the programme notice could be updated.
What had not been established?
Crowd flow under narrowing access and a wet-weather operating plan.
I sketched next week's plan for the event season before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the venue grid updates.

It resets the afternoon.
The printed programme closes next month.

Yes, as a one-evening trial with its conditions stated.
I compared two options for the supplier pack tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.

Blessedly little.
